editorialNotes: Source references use PDF page numbers, which also match the printed slide numbers. The two lectures are organised together by topic.
Slide 6 gives an outdated human cell-count estimate; it is not tested. Cytoplasm is defined as the cellular contents outside the nucleus, correcting the loose wording on slide 8.
Mature neurons and cardiomyocytes have very limited regenerative capacity; the traditional permanent-cell category is used without claiming that all renewal is impossible.

CIN III is severe epithelial dysplasia, not simple metaplasia. Invasion through the basement membrane distinguishes invasive carcinoma. HPV integration is not treated as a numerical diagnostic criterion.
Fatty infiltration of muscle in the steak photograph on slide 63 is not used as a standard example of epithelial metaplasia or intracellular steatosis.

Papillomavirus research is labelled as an extension section. Persistence and cancer risk depend on virus type and context; not all HPV infections progress to cancer. The E5/MHC-I mechanism is presented as the lecture’s research model, not a universal mechanism for every HPV type.
Pathology images illustrate the lecture concepts; pictures alone are not presented as sufficient to establish a clinical diagnosis.
Normal source slides are retained in full. Visual prompt crops remove explanatory labels, and image credits refer back to the lecture source.
